blocks.text: Living in Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: On the MLS®, Northeast Maple Ridge is the label for a sub-area, and the City of Maple Ridge has not published a boundary for it. The City’s own neighbourhood list has Whonnock, Yennadon, Webster’s Corners, Town Centre, Thornhill, Silver Valley, Ruskin, Port Haney, Port Hammond and Albion/Kanaka on it, but no northeast area.

As a rough guide only, I think of it as the east side of the city, east of 240 Street to the Mission boundary, from the Fraser River flats up to the forested land near Golden Ears Park, with Dewdney Trunk Road as the main east–west road. That is my reading, not a City boundary. It overlaps my

guides. The closest official descriptions are Webster’s Corners, which the City says is near the border of Maple Ridge and Mission, just off Dewdney Trunk Road, and the City’s North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan, which covers lands in northeast Maple Ridge.

Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, wrote this page on October 17, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. The facts here are taken from the official sources named on the page. Because rules and boundaries shift, check anything important with School District 42 and the City of Maple Ridge.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: Northeast Maple Ridge at a glance
Buses on the east side Routes 701, 748 and 749

parts.t: Route 701 starts at Haney Place and goes east on Dewdney Trunk Road to 250 Street, then Smith Avenue, then 248 Street, which is Maple Ridge East. Certain weekday trips carry on without stopping to Mission City Station

Route 748, Thornhill / Haney Place, loops out of Haney Place. It follows River Road, 240 Street and McClure Drive, then Jackson Road up to 100 Avenue, 256 Street and 98 Avenue, and on to 264 Street and 268 Street. The return trip runs along 100 Avenue. Buses come about every two hours, and some pass through Port Haney Station

Ruskin / Haney Place (route 749) is a round trip between Haney Place and 280 Street at Lougheed Highway. The way out uses Dewdney Trunk Road and 284 Street, then 116 Avenue. The trip back comes along Lougheed Highway, then 272 Street, then Dewdney Trunk Road

Effective dates: 701 from January 1, 2024, 748 from April 20, 2026, and 749 from June 8, 2026. A TransLink news post dated August 24, 2026 says route 701 service improvements begin September 7, 2026, so look at the current timetable.

blocks.text: City area plan North 256 Street Industrial Lands

parts.t: Council adopted the Official Community Plan amendments on June 23, 2026
About 500 acres on both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue, with existing uses that include gravel extraction, institutional operations and civic services
The City says adopting the plan sets future land use designations but does not approve any construction or development projects

blocks.text: Official Community Plan Thornhill Urban Reserve

parts.t: Under the Official Community Plan, Thornhill is kept as an Urban Reserve for the long term. Before urban development there gets the City’s support, its population must exceed 100,000 and the existing urban area, with its residential capacity, must be nearing build-out
Until those conditions are met, the minimum parcel size for subdivision of land designated Urban Reserve is 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres)

parts.t: Visitors get a swimming area and a small sandy beach, hiking trails, canoeing and fishing, and a playground completed in March 2025. The lake is stocked with rainbow trout each year

blocks.text: City park Thornhill Park and Thornhill Trails

parts.t: Thornhill Park is at 26007 98 Avenue and has a tone pole disc golf course, a community hall, a playground and a tennis court
Per the City’s neighbourhoods page, the 256 Street network for mountain biking and hiking has 17 trails. Their rating is moderately difficult, and a run through one typically takes an hour
Thornhill Trails is at 10390 256 Street. The City completed a 24-stall parking lot there in summer 2023

blocks.text: Metro Vancouver Kanaka Creek Regional Park

parts.t: TransLink lists the park at 11450 256 Street, Maple Ridge

items.t: 400 hectares of park along 12 kilometres of Kanaka Creek

parts.t: Canyon Trail goes 1.2 km one way from the fish hatchery to Cliff Falls, and it has a few challenging hills. Riverfront Trails are flat and 3 km one way
Metro Vancouver says the cliffs at Cliff Falls are steep and slippery and asks visitors to stay out of the creek and canyon there

blocks.text: BC Parks Golden Ears Provincial Park

parts.t: Golden Ears sits 11 km north of Maple Ridge. To drive there, take Dewdney Trunk Road, turn onto 232nd Street, and at the traffic circle turn onto Fern Crescent
The park dates from 1927 and is named for the twin peaks of Mount Blanshard
People come here to swim, windsurf, water-ski, canoe, boat and fish. Canoes and kayaks are available to rent at the Alouette (South Beach) day-use area when the weather allows

The City says Webster’s Corners features a network of trails for mountain bikers in the BCIT Woodlot

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers about 500 acres on both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue. Council adopted the Official Community Plan amendments on June 23, 2026.

Thornhill is designated a long-term Urban Reserve in the Official Community Plan. Urban development there is off the table until Maple Ridge has more than 100,000 residents and the residential capacity inside the existing urban area is nearly used up.

Before urban development can happen in the Thornhill Urban Reserve, the OCP requires approval of an amended Regional Context Statement by the Metro Vancouver Board, approval of an extension to the Fraser Sewerage Area by the Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District Board, and an area plan adopted by Council.
Until then, land designated Urban Reserve can only be subdivided into parcels of at least 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres).
The City adopted updates to the Official Community Plan in November 2025.

ALR: the sources I found include no official statement that Agricultural Land Reserve land falls within Northeast Maple Ridge taken as a whole. Because ALR status is decided one parcel at a time, check the address itself against the Agricultural Land Commission map.
The City’s Official Community Plan has policies meant to support and encourage farming on land that sits in the Agricultural Land Reserve.

Two floodplain maps are published by the City: the Fraser River Floodplain Map and the North and South Alouette River Floodplain Map. A floodplain map, the City explains, shows where flooding is expected on average once in 200 years.
Rainfall and water levels on the Fraser River, Kanaka Creek and the North and South Alouette River are monitored by the City.
According to the City, landslides and debris flows are a risk in some parts of Maple Ridge, and landslides can be triggered when snowpacks melt in warm weather.
The City names no flood or slope area covering Northeast Maple Ridge as a whole, as far as I could find, so look at the City’s maps for the specific address.

Chapter 3 of the Official Community Plan holds the City’s lot-size guide for rural designations. Generally, Rural Residential lots are 0.8 hectares (about 2 acres) with community water available, or 2.0 hectares (about 4.9 acres) with water on site.

There is no West Coast Express station in Northeast Maple Ridge. Maple Ridge has two West Coast Express stops: Maple Meadows Station, then Port Haney Station. Five trips run daily, Monday to Friday, heading out of Maple Ridge each morning and coming back each evening.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Northeast Maple Ridge

parts.t: Check the Urban Reserve and the zone.
If the property is in Thornhill, ask the City what the Urban Reserve policy means for subdividing or building on that parcel.
Check the water, septic and access.
Find out who supplies the water, request the well and septic records, and look into how you get to the property in winter.
Check the ALR on larger lots.
Before planning anything on farmland, search the address on the Agricultural Land Commission’s map.
Check the slope and flood maps.
Ask the City what the floodplain, creek and slope rules mean for the exact address.
Ask SD42 for the exact address.
Inspect the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring. If the home has a well, get the water tested.

blocks.text: Northeast Maple Ridge questions

parts.t: Northeast Maple Ridge is the name of an MLS® sub-area. A boundary for it isn’t published by the City of Maple Ridge.
As a rough guide I think of it as the east side of the city, east of 240 Street to the Mission boundary, but that is my reading, not a City boundary. It overlaps my
How do I get around from Northeast Maple Ridge?

Heading east from Haney Place on Dewdney Trunk Road, route 701 reaches Maple Ridge East by way of 250 Street, Smith Avenue and 248 Street. A few weekday trips go on to Mission City Station without stopping.

Thornhill / Haney Place, route 748, is a loop that begins at Haney Place. It runs out on River Road, 240 Street and McClure Drive, and Jackson Road takes it to 100 Avenue, then on through 256 Street and 98 Avenue, then 264 Street and 268 Street, before it returns along 100 Avenue. Buses come roughly every two hours, and some call at Port Haney Station.

Route 749 (Ruskin / Haney Place) travels from Haney Place out to 280 Street at Lougheed Highway, then returns. The outbound route is Dewdney Trunk Road, then 284 Street, then 116 Avenue; the return is by Lougheed Highway and 272 Street, finishing on Dewdney Trunk Road.

Timetable effective dates are January 1, 2024 for 701, April 20, 2026 for 748 and June 8, 2026 for 749. According to TransLink’s news post of August 24, 2026, route 701 gets service improvements starting September 7, 2026. Check the current timetable.

No West Coast Express station serves Northeast Maple Ridge. The two stops in Maple Ridge are Port Haney Station and Maple Meadows Station. There are five trips a day, Monday to Friday, which leave Maple Ridge in the morning and come back in the evening.
Which schools are in Northeast Maple Ridge?

The Province’s school list shows Garibaldi Secondary at 24789 Dewdney Trunk Road, Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary at 10445 245 Street, Webster’s Corners Elementary at 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road and Whonnock Elementary at 27471 112 Avenue. Blue Mountain Elementary is at 12153 248th Street on the school’s own SD42 site.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
What parks and library are there?
Whonnock Lake Park is at 27871 113 Avenue, Webster’s Corners Park is at 25496 Dewdney Trunk Road and Thornhill Trails is at 10390 256 Street.
Maple Ridge has a single Fraser Valley Regional Library branch. It is the Maple Ridge Public Library, located at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road.
What plans cover Northeast Maple Ridge?
The City’s North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan was adopted on June 23, 2026, and the Official Community Plan holds Thornhill as a long-term Urban Reserve.
I found no neighbourhood area plan for Northeast Maple Ridge as a whole.
Is Northeast Maple Ridge in a floodplain or on a slope?

The City has two floodplain maps, one for the Fraser River and one for the North and South Alouette River. In the City’s words, a floodplain map marks the area that is expected to flood about once every 200 years on average.
Some areas of Maple Ridge are exposed to landslides and debris flows, the City says. It adds that warm weather melting the snowpack can bring on landslides.
Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
What are the homes and lots like?

The City calls Thornhill a heavily forested, mainly residential area with several farms and nurseries, and says Whonnock is a rural residential area where many people have horses and small tree and fruit farms.
ALR status is set parcel by parcel, so check the exact address on the
. I don’t have lot-size data for this area.
